leading_positions.synthesis: Three of eight members explicitly prefer Car-Parrinello first-principles molecular dynamics (B024) as their round-1 configuration, all with Michele Parrinello and Roberto Car, but with different citation wording (Aqvist: unifying electronic-structure theory and MD for bonding and reactions in condensed phases; Brzezinski and Linke: unification of electronic structure with atomic motion). They share the view that the attribution (a single two-author 1985 paper) and maturity are unusually clean. They differ on how far the citation should reach beyond 1985 (Aqvist and Linke raise this as an open question; Brzezinski would anchor strictly on the 1985 step) and on whether later work such as metadynamics should matter. The main objections from the other five members are not about merit but about centre of gravity (condensed-phase physics and materials versus chemistry), recent computational prizes (2013, 2024), and whether theory should rank above experimental discoveries with direct reach into medicine.

Two members explicitly prefer ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B064) with the same trio, Pieter Cullis, Michael Hope and Thomas Madden, and similar citations on ionizable lipids enabling delivery of nucleic-acid medicines. Daniel Aili emphasizes clinical consequence and the pKa-tuned design principle; Emma Sparr frames it as lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour. They differ on the margin: Sparr's opening proposal paired Cullis with Anderson, which Aili and Aqvist question, since the ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing work is Vancouver-centred while Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid screening. Both flag that six credited names, academic and company contributions, and the 2023 Medicine prize make the credit and disciplinary framing contentious.

One member (Chabes) prefers massively parallel DNA sequencing by synthesis (B012) with a two-person Solexa citation, Shankar Balasubramanian and David Klenerman. Aili and Linke list B012 as an alternative and recognize its impact, but Aili's own ballot includes Jonathan Rothberg, and Aqvist, Brzezinski and Somfai raise the competing 454, Ju terminator and Mayer clonal-array routes as an unresolved attribution problem. Chabes names B024 as his fallback if attribution cannot be settled.

One member (Somfai) prefers palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (B006) with Stephen Buchwald and John Hartwig. Others (Chabes, Linke) accept its maturity and the clean pair but question how conceptually distinct it is from the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize; Somfai argues C-N coupling required different mechanistic solutions. Kosugi's earlier precedent is a minor attribution question.

One member (Zou) prefers rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts (B030) with Avelino Corma, Mark Davis and Stacey Zones. Zou states that no colleague ranked it in the opening, and that it is a field rather than a single dated discovery, with industrial priority questions and omitted academic contributors (Tsapatsis, Yu). Brzezinski notes the same diffuseness concern.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's first-choice configuration is a single prize part; no member proposed a two-part prize in round 1, and Brzezinski explicitly notes that the three-person limit makes a method-plus-mechanism pairing difficult.

B024 is acknowledged by members beyond its three supporters (Aili, Sparr, Somfai, Zou, Chabes) as mature, widely used and cleanly attributed to Car and Parrinello; the disagreement is about category and significance, not about maturity or credit.

B012 and B046 are repeatedly named as strong alternatives (B012 by Aili, Brzezinski and Linke; B046 by Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Somfai and Sparr), and the consequence of B064 is not disputed by those who rank it lower.
Members across positions accept that the committee's choice will depend on balancing attribution cleanliness against reach and category fit.
scientific_disputes: Whether Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics is chemistry or computational and condensed-matter physics (raised by Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke against their own preference, and by Somfai and Zou), and whether the 2013 multiscale and 2024 structure-prediction prizes make computational methods already covered.

Whether quantitative accuracy of plane-wave DFT with fictitious-mass dynamics (Aqvist's question to Zou, and Linke's own note about displacement by Born-Oppenheimer MD and machine-learned potentials) affects how the 1985 contribution should be described.

Whether ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B064) are core chemistry (pKa-tuned design, non-bilayer phase behaviour) or pharmaceutical formulation, given the 2023 Medicine prize (Aili, Sparr against Aqvist, Linke, Chabes).

Whether sequencing by synthesis (B012) is chemistry with a distinct reversible-terminator principle or a platform and instrument technology, given the 1980 Sanger and Gilbert prize (Chabes, Aqvist, Sparr, Aili).
Whether C-N cross-coupling (B006) is a conceptual advance over the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize or a follow-on (Somfai against Chabes and Linke).
attribution_disputes: B064: six credited names across Vancouver (Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan), MIT (Anderson, Langer) and company teams; Aili and Sparr both choose Cullis, Hope and Madden, but Sparr's opening paired Cullis with Anderson, and Aqvist, Aili and Chabes press the cut.

B012: whether the citation is Balasubramanian and Klenerman only (Chabes) or includes Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing), Ju (terminator chemistry) or Mayer (clonal arrays); Aili's ballot includes Rothberg, Chabes notes he has not verified the invention chronology, and Linke raised that 454 uses a different chemical route.
B046: crowded credit among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa and others, with PROTACs and molecular glues as potentially separate discoveries (Aili, Aqvist).
B030: Tsapatsis and Yu are only partly separable from the three named zeolite laureates, and early industrial work (Union Carbide, Mobil) raises priority questions (Zou, Brzezinski).
B024: the pair is uncontested, but whether Parrinello's later metadynamics and ML potential work should appear in a citation is open (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke).
maturity_disputes: B046 (targeted protein degradation): Aili and Linke treat the mechanism as well confirmed but clinical proof as still maturing.
B025 (biomolecular condensates): Sparr lists it as an alternative but questions whether debate about in vivo phase separation makes it premature.
B064: the 2023 Medicine prize makes the timing question one of redundancy rather than immaturity (Aili, Sparr).
B024: no member disputes maturity, and the open point is whether recognition is overdue or whether recent computational prizes (2013, 2024) argue for waiting.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Heiner Linke (chair) discloses that as a physicist he may favour a physical idea and that B024 is his own first choice; he is also the author of this process summary.
Johan Aqvist discloses that as a simulation specialist he may overvalue theory relative to experimental discoveries (B024).
Emma Sparr discloses her own field is lipid self-assembly and that she must not favour B064 for that reason.
Peter Brzezinski notes that B024 touches his field of biological energy conversion indirectly and that B068 (Gray, Winkler) has only his opening vote.

No member disclosed a personal collaboration, institutional tie or formal recusal request with any candidate; Chabes notes that sequencing is close to his own field and says he judges its impact from use.
questions_for_round2: Is B024 chemistry for the purposes of this prize, and if so, can the citation be fixed to the 1985 unification of electronic structure and ionic motion without adjudicating later work, given the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes?

For B064, which of Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer would a three-person citation include, and on what documented basis (ionizable-lipid design, rapid-mixing assembly, lipidoid screening) is priority decided?

For B012, can a Balasubramanian and Klenerman citation be defended against the Rothberg, Ju and Mayer routes, and does the reversible-terminator chemistry make it a chemistry prize in light of the 1980 Sanger and Gilbert prize?

Should B046 (named as an alternative by six members) be raised to a full candidacy, and if so which discovery (PROTACs or molecular glues) and which laureates, given the maturity concern about clinical proof?

Should the committee weigh clean attribution and maturity (B024, B006) above reach into medicine and biology (B064, B012, B046), and can any member state what would make them move their first choice to another ballot ID?
For B006 and B030, what evidence shows the C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 prize and that zeolite design can be cited as a single discovery rather than a field?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a plurality of three for B024 and a split of the remaining five first choices across four different ballot IDs (B064 two, B012, B006, B030 one each), so no ballot has the five votes needed for a majority. The leading candidacy is distinguished mainly by clean attribution, while the other leading candidacies are distinguished by reach into medicine and biology and are held back by credit allocation. Round 2 should settle the category question for B024 and the three-person cut for B064 and B012, and test whether B046 can become a first choice.
